requirements.requirement: curl package is held at its current installed version (7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19) on node1
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed the installed curl version, ran 'sudo apt-mark hold curl' (returned 'curl set on hold.'), and verified curl appears in apt-mark showhold output and dpkg selections show 'hold'. Post-restart re-check (dpkg -l shows 'hi' status flag) confirms the hold is durable, not just applied and forgotten.

requirements.requirement: A system update (dist-upgrade) leaves curl at its current version, i.e. does not attempt to upgrade it
requirements.summary: After apt-get update, a dist-upgrade dry-run (--simulate) was run and grepped for curl, returning no match (grep exit 1) even though many other packages were listed as being configured/upgraded. apt-cache policy also shows the candidate version equals the installed version, and post-reboot the dry-run again excludes curl, directly demonstrating the hold is effective against the package manager's upgrade path.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied both material outcomes of the task: curl was placed on apt-mark hold at its currently installed version, and a dist-upgrade dry-run directly confirmed curl is excluded from the upgrade set both before and after a full node reboot, showing the hold persists across a restart. The reboot cycle (boot_id 9094f607... -> c66c32d0...) also satisfies the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol with a clean pre/post transition and no residue. All commands are read-only checks or narrowly scoped, purposeful mutations directly tied to the task or the restart protocol.
limitations: prepare phase was disabled/aliased to before_prepare, so there is no distinct after_prepare snapshot to separate preparer-created state from executor changes; the before/after_executor comparison was used instead.
No evidence of data or cluster-state recovery checks post-reboot beyond curl hold and package status, since this single-node task has no cluster/data service in scope.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command has a clear purpose: apt-mark hold curl (the task's core action), apt-get update (necessary prerequisite for a meaningful dist-upgrade simulation), and the reboot (shutdown -r now) which is part of the separate provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol rather than an unnecessary mutation, since it was bounded, non-destructive, and used only to demonstrate persistence of the hold. The dist-upgrade commands were run with -s (simulate/dry-run) and did not actually mutate installed packages. Lifecycle diffs show only expected reboot artifacts (new boot_id, new systemd-private temp dirs replacing old ones) with no leftover files, no failed services, and unchanged package-health status before and after. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
